rationale: mutation_score=0.571 is below the 0.5 threshold boundary acceptance is fine numerically but three requirements (FR2, FR3, SR2) are uncovered per validation_report's uncovered_requirements list, and the mutation_baseline_run passes cleanly (exit_code 0) so the golden is not at fault. Inspecting the actual mutant content: the FR2 mutant (fr2_scope_narrowed_operator_swap) genuinely broadens the trigger_condition to claim the anomaly affects all nmi=1 cases instead of only irq=111, which is a real, observable misreport that FR2's check should catch but does not. The FR3 mutant (fr3_ordinary_priority_finding_misreported_condition_negation) genuinely fabricates a false ordinary-priority violation (claims irq[2] wrongly beats irq[0]) that contradicts the actual correct RTL behavior, which FR3's check should catch but does not. The SR2 mutant (sr2_wrong_affected_signal_domain_specific) genuinely misreports the affected signal as grant[2] instead of grant[1] and omits the grant[3] suppression claim, which SR2's check should catch but does not. All three mutants are valid corruptions of observable, checkable claims -- the evaluator's FR2/FR3 checks are vacuous (per analyzer: they only fire on optional regex-matched explicit claims and pass by default when absent) and SR2's check, despite looking well-constructed in code, is not actually being exercised to fail on this mutant. This is an evaluation_framework defect, not a mutant defect.
revision_instructions: Strengthen evaluate.py so FR2, FR3, and SR2 checks are behaviorally discriminating rather than vacuously passing. FR2 must actively verify, for the SR1-matching finding (and any other findings scoped to nmi=1), that the reported scope of the anomaly is confined to the specific trigger condition (nmi=1 AND irq=3'b111) rather than a broader or narrower claim; if a finding's trigger_condition text asserts the anomaly holds for nmi=1 regardless of irq value (or for any nmi=1 case other than irq=111), FR2 must FAIL, since this contradicts the requirement that grant[3]=1/grant[2:0]=000 holds uniformly for nmi=1 except at irq=111. This check must not silently pass when no explicit scope claim is present in a way that lets an incorrect broad claim slip through -- it must parse the actual trigger_condition text of matching findings and compare the asserted scope against the pinned ground-truth scope (exactly one of 8 irq patterns under nmi=1). FR3 must actively verify that any finding claiming an anomaly in the nmi=0 ordinary-priority path is checked against the real fixed-priority policy (irq[0] > irq[1] > irq[2]); if a finding asserts an ordinary-priority violation (e.g. claims irq[2] outranks irq[0], or any reordering) that does not match the true priority relationship, FR3 must FAIL by flagging the finding as incorrect, rather than accepting any well-formed prose about the nmi=0 path uncritically. SR2 must be verified to actually fail when the affected_signal field of the SR1-matching finding names a signal other than grant[1]/grant[3] (e.g. grant[2]) or omits the grant[3]-suppression claim; add a concrete test invocation of the SR2 check function against a submission whose affected_signal field is wrong, confirming it emits FAIL, and fix whatever logic gap currently allows it to pass despite the mismatch (e.g. it may be matching on a substring or fallback pattern too loosely, or not being reached before an early return). All three checks must be behavioral: judge the submitted finding text against the pinned ground-truth trigger scope and pinned ground-truth affected-signal identity, not against superficial keyword presence.
